summary: Evaluate the J=8 rational-pole kinetic 3x3 tensor and dispersion determinant, including complex kx and zero kz.

capability: Evaluate the J=8 rational-pole kinetic 3x3 tensor and dispersion determinant, including complex kx and zero kz.
operation: evaluate the Ronnmark kinetic dispersion tensor
SI species and wavepoint to Ronnmark K, D and determinant
discovery.boundary: zero kz is allowed without the conventional sum's positive clamp

identity.relation: SI species and wavepoint to Ronnmark K, D and determinant
identity.direction: SI species and wavepoint to Ronnmark K, D and determinant
identity.definition: Replace the Z and harmonic response by J=8 resonance poles and the Ronnmark R function, add Maxwell curl terms, and compute det(D).
identity.coordinates: wavevector x-z plane; complex kx permitted, z parallel to B0
identity.boundary: zero kz is allowed without the conventional sum's positive clamp
assumptions: Input units and normalization follow the declared ports; no physical parameters are inferred.

inputs.name: B0
inputs.description: Background magnetic-field strength, setting the cyclotron frequency and entering the pole-resonance argument
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonzero; the cyclotron frequency is proportional to B0.

inputs.name: qs
inputs.description: Species charges, setting the signs of the cyclotron frequency and the coupling terms
inputs.constraints: Finite; element count matches the other species arrays.

inputs.name: ms
inputs.description: Species masses, entering the thermal speed and the cyclotron frequency

inputs.name: ns0
inputs.description: Species absolute number densities, entering the plasma frequency

inputs.name: Ts0
inputs.description: Species temperatures, already converted to kelvin under the source convention

inputs.name: f
inputs.description: Electromagnetic-wave frequency, converted to angular frequency and then entering the resonance argument

inputs.name: omega
inputs.description: Directly supplied angular frequency that can replace `f` in the resonance argument (preserving the source runtime's original angular-frequency token and avoiding the round trip through `2*pi*f`)
inputs.constraints: Optional keyword argument, default `None`; exactly one of `omega` and `f` must be supplied; when `omega` is given its value is used directly as $\omega$ and `f` is ignored, and it must be finite and nonzero.

inputs.name: kz
inputs.description: Wavevector component parallel to the magnetic field, entering the resonance argument and multiplying the thermal speed
inputs.constraints: Finite; zero is allowed (source case 2 uses `kz=0.0`), in which case $n_z=0$ and the parallel resonance argument reduces to $\omega/\omega_{cs}$.

inputs.name: kx
inputs.description: Wavevector component perpendicular to the magnetic field, giving $b=(k_\perp\rho_{cs})^2$ and the refractive index
inputs.constraints: Finite; complex values correspond to the source fsolve solving in the complex kx plane, where $b$ has an imaginary part.

outputs.name: K
outputs.shape: `(3, 3)` complex matrix with component-axis order x, y, z
outputs.constraints: Finite complex; antisymmetric pairs satisfy $K_{yx}=-K_{xy}$ and $K_{zy}=-K_{yz}$.

outputs.name: D
outputs.description: Dispersion tensor including the Maxwell curl term
outputs.shape: `(3, 3)` complex matrix with component-axis order x, y, z

outputs.name: determinant
outputs.description: Dispersion determinant $\mathcal{D}=\det D$, whose zeros give the eigenmodes

outputs.name: omega
outputs.description: Angular frequency converted from the input frequency

outputs.name: as
outputs.description: Species $a_s=k_\perp\rho_{cs}$, the scale of the pole-coupling term $\sqrt2 a_s c_j/x_{sj}$
outputs.constraints: Finite; can be positive or negative for real kx, and is complex for complex kx with no sign order defined.

outputs.name: b
outputs.constraints: Nonnegative real for real kx; complex for complex kx, with no nonnegativity order defined.

outputs.name: bzj
outputs.description: $J=8$ pole residues weighting the resonance term of each pole
outputs.constraints: Finite complex; the second half is the conjugate of the first half.

outputs.name: czj
outputs.description: $J=8$ pole positions giving the complex resonance offsets
outputs.constraints: Finite complex; the second half is the negative conjugate of the first half.

outputs.name: j_order
outputs.description: Pole order, echoed so the resonance-block size can be checked

outputs.name: branches
outputs.description: Ronnmark branch label taken by each (species, pole) combination, used to check method-selector coverage

outputs.name: tensor_convention
outputs.description: Text label for the tensor convention

preconditions: Species arrays are finite, non-empty and shape-compatible; masses, densities and temperatures are positive, with nonzero charge and magnetic field.
The wavepoint and derived frequency/scales are finite and satisfy the selected numerical path domain.
supported: Evaluate the J=8 rational-pole kinetic 3x3 tensor and dispersion determinant, including complex kx and zero kz.
excluded: Mode identification, root finding and accuracy outside the tested finite-harmonic or rational-pole approximation.
Inputs that violate the numerical domain or require a different tensor convention.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for declared invalid inputs; numeric conversion errors may propagate for unsupported Python objects.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical backend errors propagate; no fallback relation is substituted.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative root solve is exposed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping is returned after an exception.

python.signature: evaluate_kinetic_dispersion_ronnmark(*, B0, qs, ms, ns0, Ts0, f=None, kz, kx, omega=None)

example.description: Evaluate the J=8 Ronnmark tensor at zero parallel wavenumber.
example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_kinetic_dispersion_ronnmark
r=evaluate_kinetic_dispersion_ronnmark(B0=1.0, qs=[-1.60217662e-19], ms=[9.1094e-31], ns0=[6.075e19], Ts0=[11604941.036704937],omega=1e11,kz=0,kx=1e4); assert r['D'].shape==(3,3)
example.expected: Observed PASS: the zero-kz case returns finite 3x3 K and D tensors, a determinant, J=8 pole tables and the tensor convention.
